reason: UCR has genuine ancient-world study: global ancient craft/material culture, early-democratic Greek archaeology and Athenian democracy, classical and cross-cultural myth, ancient passages in philosophy, political thought, empire and warfare. These contributions remain sound. They do not establish the sustained ancient Mediterranean/Near-Eastern cultural-historical and textual/material source inquiry that defines this degree and its Ancient History specialisation. The proposed 24-course programme gives six heritage/art courses and five literature courses the appearance of ancient-world depth, although Renaissance Italy, modern museums, art historiography since the sixteenth century, general literary interpretation and modern film adaptation have different taught objects. Four rhetoric/communication courses are primarily skills, stylistics, contemporary persuasion and principally Dutch work with primary-school children; their classical origins do not turn all 30 EC into classical studies. The only advanced History Research Seminar actually investigates Walcheren in 1809, not an ancient topic. Greek Archaeology and Heritage and Ancient Democracy have substantial overlapping early-Greek democratic content, so counting both cannot supply missing Near-Eastern/Roman/social-historical breadth. Broad empires/warfare surveys preserve real ancient content, but do not supply the defining study of ancient evidence, religion, Roman change, ordinary ancient lives and a specialised ancient research progression. Replacing modern companions with other modern history, art, sociology or media courses changes the inquiry to general cultural heritage or humanities. Archaeology reconstruction still lacks a sustained archaeological theory/methods/cult/city/death sequence; language specialisations lack acquisition and original-language text progression; Near-Eastern reconstruction lacks Akkadian/cuneiform and Mesopotamian progression. A coherent 180-EC UCR humanities programme is therefore not enough to support a comparable alternative here. This judgment concerns the defining substance and progression, not a matching quota, title, isolated absent course, professional licence or the mere absence of an ancient language from the selected Ancient History route.
